build_inputs.angles:
1. Open on the number and the record together: 523 horsepower and 479 pound-feet from a 3.0-litre twin-turbo straight-six, in the fastest compact car ever to lap the Nurburgring. That is the most powerful M2 there has ever been.

2. The argument the whole video rests on, and it is the one the comments will have: this is automatic only. No manual, at any price. The last M2 CS came standard with a six-speed manual - BMW's own press release called it the first CS model to be fitted with one as standard - and the ordinary, far cheaper M2 still offers three pedals today. So the most expensive, most focused M2 ever built is the one you cannot have a manual in, and the cheap one is the one you can. Argue it honestly both ways: the eight-speed is unquestionably quicker, and that is exactly the trade people are angry about.

3. The record, with the numbers that make it mean something: seven minutes twenty-five point five around the Nordschleife, driven by BMW's own Jorg Weidinger in April 2025. It beat the Audi RS3's seven thirty-three, and it is thirteen seconds faster than the standard M2's lap - same driver, same track, two years apart. Do not call it a BMW record outright, because the M4 CSL is still quicker at seven eighteen; it is the compact-car record.

4. The money beat, and it is the uncomfortable one: this costs about ninety-nine thousand seven hundred dollars with destination. That is around nine thousand more than an M4 Competition and thirty-three thousand more than a standard M2. You are paying a premium over the bigger, faster car to get the smaller one. Read this car's own asking price off the listing and use that if it differs.

5. Cover the catch honestly. It is a two-series at six figures, it is rear-drive only, and the weight saving everybody quotes is about thirty kilos of carbon - real, but it is still a three-thousand-seven-hundred-pound car. Reviewers have pointed out it loses things an ordinary M2 has. Be specific about what living with it is actually like rather than vague.

6. Close on the question: would you pay more than an M4 costs for the quickest M2 ever made, knowing you can never shift it yourself - or buy the cheaper M2 with the manual and let it be slower?

script: A 3.0-liter twin-turbo straight-six with 523 horsepower and 479 pound-feet took the Nürburgring compact-car record without a clutch pedal. In 2020 the BMW M2 CS became BMW's first CS with a six-speed manual as standard. Now it's eight-speed automatic only. With the stock splitter, Jörg Weidinger ran 7:25.5 in April 2025, thirteen seconds faster than his standard M2 lap. Up front, you've got six pistons in each caliper. Only the rear wheels get power, and BMW retuned the active differential specifically for the CS. The most powerful M2 runs an S58 with iron sprayed straight onto the cylinder walls. The cheaper M2 still comes with three pedals, but BMW clocks it at 4.1 to sixty against 3.7 here. It was about $100,000 new and they go for about $100,000 today, so would you take the Nürburgring record setter or the cheaper M2 with a stick?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2026 BMW M2 CS, finished in BMW Individual Velvet Blue Metallic with a Black interior. The odometer on this M2 CS currently displays approximately 842 miles. This M2 CS is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this M2 CS cost $103,785 new. A partial list of notable equipment includes M Compound brakes, MP carbon antenna, M Carbon roof, and heated M Carbon bucket seats. The seller reports no notable modifications. The M2 CS is the lightweight, higher-output version of the G87-generation BMW M2, and it was built for the 2026 model year only. Compared to the standard M2, the CS adds 50 horsepower and uses carbon fiber-reinforced plastic body panels and forged wheels to reduce weight by nearly 100 pounds. Production reportedly totaled 2,882 units worldwide, including 770 for the U.S. market. Power comes from a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged inline-6, rated at about 523 horsepower and 479 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via an 8-speed automatic transmission.
